full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to and confirmation of possession in the suit land. According to the plaintiff their father Osman Mondal was owner of /8/- annas of the tenancy recorded in khatian No. 736 of  mouza Sadipur. He transferred the suit land along with other last by executing pasta Ext. 1 dated 17.3.56 in favour defendant Nos. 1 and 3 by way of security for loan of Rs.150/. Plaintiffs Inherited the land from their father and repaid the consideration on 21.7.62. They got back the land but the defendants did not return the patta. During the Rent-roll operation the disputed property was recorded in the name of defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 1 threes tend plaintiff to dispossess the property Chaitra, 1372 B S. In the above circumstances the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit on the ground that Osman Mondal learned out the disputed land to defendant No. by Patta Ext. 1 dated 17.1.56 and delivered, possession to them. They paid rent to Osman Mondal and later on to the Government Acquired Estate on receipt of dakhilad, They noticed the allegation of the plaintiffs. 

 4. The learned Munsif considered the case on merit and held that the lease by Ext. 1 is null and void under the provision of section 75(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as it was made after 16.12.55 Nevertheless the trial Court found that defendants paid rent to the Government and Governments recognised defendants as tenants and that names of the defendants have been records in the Rent roll. In this view of the matter the trial Court held that plaintiff is not called to any relief in the suit. Therefore, he dismissed the suit. 

 Mr. Moazzem Hossein the learned Advocate for the respondents, submits that lease given by Ext 1, the patta, has been found null and void and as such the land goes back to the plaintiff, the owner of the land. The land was not forfeited by Government as there was no such provision at that time in the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act that the forfeiture clause was inserted in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by section 3 of EP Act IV of 1956 which came into force on 26.9.56 In the above circumstances tip lower appellate Court rightly held that plaintiff is entitled to a decree in she suit as the land reverted to its original owner, the plaintiff, who are heirs of late Osman Mondal.
